questions.q:
Assertion (A) Two condensers of same capacity are connected first in parallel and then in series. The ratio of resultant capacities in the two cases will be $4: 1$.
Reason ( $R$ ) In parallel, capacity increases and in series capacity decreases.
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is a correct explanation for $\mathrm{A}$.
Both $A$ and $R$ are true but $R$ is not a correct explanation for A.
questions.solution:
Given, two capacitors of same capacities $C$.
In series, equivalent capacitance is given by
$\begin{aligned} & \frac{1}{C_S}=\frac{1}{C_1}+\frac{1}{C_2}=\frac{1}{C}+\frac{1}{C}=\frac{2}{C} \\ & C_S=\frac{C}{2}\end{aligned}$
In parallel, equivalent capacitance is given by
$C_P=C_1+C_2=C+C=2 C$
Ratio $=\frac{C_P}{C_S}=\frac{2 C}{\left(\frac{C}{2}\right)}=\frac{4}{1}\Rightarrow \quad C_P: C_S=4: 1$
Hence, Assertion is true
In parallel, $C_P>C$
In series, $C_S < C$
So, in parallel, capacity is increased but in series, capacity is decreased.
Hence, Reason is also true, but it is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

Reason R : Capacitance of metallic spheres depend on the radii of spheres.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
questions.solution:
Potential of a conducting sphere is given by V=KQR 

As in case of metallic sphere either solid or hollow, the charge will reside on the surface of the sphere. Since both spheres have same surface area, so they can hold equal charge.

∴Q1=Q2

The capacitance of a metallic sphere depends only on its radius. It does not matter whether the sphere is hollow or solid.

Hence, A is false but R is true.

Match the column-I with column-II.
\(\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|}
\hline
& \text{Column-I} & & \text{Column-II} \\
\hline
A. & \text{Capacity of parallel plate} \\ 
  & \text{air capacitor, } C_0 \text{ is} & p. & \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d-t} \\
\hline
B. & \text{Capacity when dielectric} \\ 
  & \text{medium fills the entire space} & q. & \frac{K \epsilon_0 A}{d} \\
\hline
C. & \text{Capacity when dielectric of} \\ 
  & \text{thickness } t  < d \text{ fills the space} & r. & \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d - t \left(1 - \frac{1}{K}\right)} \\
\hline
D. & \text{Capacity when conductor of} \\ 
  & \text{thickness } t < d \text{ fills the space} & s. & \frac{\epsilon_0 A}{d} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
(A) \(C_0^{\prime}=\frac{E_0 / d}{d}\)
\(\varepsilon_0{ }^{\text {ma }}\) permittivity of medium
(B) \(C=\frac{K \varepsilon_0 A}{d}\)
\(K=\) dielectric constant of medium
